## Standards

No hard documented-standard violation found. Reviewer Soul remains free of runtime/schema mechanics, and no permanent probe was added.

- **Judgement call — possible Primitive Obsession:** `src/reviewer-agent.ts:83-91` derives domain failure categories from message text:
  > `if (/provider|model|auth/.test(text)) return "provider";`

  Prefer typed execution errors carrying `ReviewerFailureClassification`; wording changes can otherwise silently alter evidence.

- **Judgement call — possible Repeated Switches:** `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:295-405` repeatedly branches on:
  > `proposal.spec.state === "established"`

  The same discriminant controls selections, grants, prompt creation, and evidence projection. Normalize the proposal state once, then compile the normalized shape.

- **Judgement call — possible Duplicated Code:** pin freezing is independently implemented in `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:247-249` and `src/reviewer-pinned-git.ts:29-31`:
  > `function immutablePin(...)`

  Export one implementation. The current shallow `Object.freeze({ ...pin.refs })` versus `immutableReviewerRefs(...)` difference demonstrates drift risk.

- **Judgement call — possible Mysterious Name:** `test/reviewer-role.test.ts:21-28` uses terse callback names such as `n`, `t`, `f`, and `x`; prefer `name`, `tool`, `handler`, and `request`.

## Spec

1. **P1 — Repository-root pinning is implemented incorrectly** (`src/reviewer-pinned-git.ts:39-42`, `src/reviewer-agent.ts:204-206`).

   Spec:
   > “`preflight.git.pin-target`: identify repository root and pin HEAD commit…”

   The reader records `realpath(root)` as `repositoryRoot` rather than discovering Git’s top-level directory. When Reviewer is launched from a repository subdirectory, preflight Git commands still succeed through parent discovery, but the accepted pin contains that subdirectory. Post-acceptance execution then attempts `git clone --mirror <subdirectory>`, which is not itself a repository and fails after the irreversible transition. This prevents otherwise valid nested-directory invocations and incorrectly turns a root-identification defect into post-acceptance infrastructure failure.

No scope creep identified.

**Summary:** Standards: 4 judgement-call findings; worst is possible Primitive Obsession in message-text failure classification. Spec: 1 finding; worst is P1 repository-root pinning.
